LESSON: WRITING 9.4.1 PUNCTUATION (THE COMMA)

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.4: Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation (The comma)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation (The comma), part of Strand 9 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: which the comma is used and then • write down some sentences on a digital device with assistive technology. Why do you think we use a comma when writing?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

1. identify commas from writings on wall charts/board/digital and print/braille resources.

3. use commas to write lists of items/names.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. identify commas from writings on wall charts/board/digital and print/braille resources.
2. use the comma correctly in written exercises with peers.
3. use commas to write lists of items/names.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation (The comma) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration -as they engage in group practice exercises to write using a comma.

• Digital literacy –is enhanced as the learner writes sentences with commas on digital devices with assistive technology.

Values:
Responsibility as learners takes up roles during role play activities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Citizenship (social cohesion) - as learners work together to identify commas in lists and sentences.

Links to other Learning Areas:
Use of commas is emphasised in Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities.
